correctness.rationale: Independent Catalan erasure of one or two nonadjacent ear triangles gives p=C(n-3)/C(n-2) and q=C(n-4)/C(n-2). Direct covariance K=(p-q)I-qA+(q-p^2)J and unitary DFT yield the complete spectrum; its constant eigenvalue has the exact rational factor (n-5)(n-4)(n-1)/[2(2n-7)(2n-5)^2]. All nonconstant eigenvalues are strictly ordered by frequency distance. The crossing sign for n=5..20 is certified by sixteen exact rational lower bounds (minimum 1069/840000), and n>=21 by the positive cubic 147t^3+5389t^2+49281t+359, t=n-21. Positive-spectrum conditioning is maximized uniquely by n=6 with 1/2 divided by 1/49=49/2, using monotonic exact bounds for other sizes. Enumerating all convex triangulations through n=11 and independently Fourier-transforming their empirical covariance was passed by the packaged checker (6100 assertions); these finite checks supplement rather than replace the all-n proof. No other normalizations are assumed.

originality.rationale: The final novel claim is the exact Fourier least-observable-mode crossover between polygon sizes 20 and 21 and the globally sharp 49/2 positive-spectrum condition bound, not the classical Catalan ear counts. The 2019 general variance theorem requires triangle weights invariant under side-length translation, which excludes complex position-dependent ear Fourier weights; the older ear marginal and total-variance results cannot directly identify the nonconstant mode order. The closest published diagonal-covariance theorems provide compatible-pair probabilities and sign information but do not order the full harmonic spectrum or certify the size crossover and condition-number maximizer. These results provide essential inputs, and deriving the frame spectrum is relatively short, so a previously unindexed sharp spectral result remains a priority risk.
residual_risks: The pairwise Catalan formulas known from older general diagonal results make the raw covariance readily derivable; the original contribution is the sharp Fourier-mode transition and all-n optimization, which may exist in older unindexed work.

value.rationale: The ear-location vector is a natural cyclic signal from uniformly random Catalan triangulations. Its minimum covariance eigenvalue controls least-squares reconstruction of cyclic ear statistics. Determining which spatial mode is intrinsically least stable and the sharp worst-case conditioning over all polygon sizes addresses meaningful observability, not a random finite invariant. The surprising shift from total ear-count fluctuations to first spatial-wave fluctuations exactly at 21 vertices, a single rank-defect pentagon, the unique worst hexagon, and limiting ratio five provide a complete family-wide spectral classification. Pair counting is short but the all-n sharp threshold/optimization requires nontrivial uniform analytic inequalities; the value claim does not rest on programming alone.
